**Late-Cycle / Transition Risk.** The US is in a **late-cycle, growth-softening regime** where residual nominal strength (inflation sticky at 3.7% PCE, ISM Manufacturing at 55.6) masks deteriorating labor momentum (NFP -23K in July), a slowing Q2 GDP print of just 1.5%, a 3m10y curve still inverted with a >30% model-implied recession probability, and a Fed that is effectively on hold at a real policy rate that remains **above neutral** — the June dot plot median of 3.375% against a long-run neutral of ~3% means real rates are still mildly restrictive against sticky inflation. A rebound toward +100K+ confirms AI-driven productivity restructuring; a second consecutive negative print shifts the conversation from "soft landing" to recession and would likely see a sharp steepening of the curve and rotation into defensives.
